vignette: A 34-year-old man presents with 2 days of a spreading, warm, tender, erythematous area on his left lower leg after a minor scrape while gardening. There is no fluctuance or purulent drainage, and bedside ultrasound shows no fluid collection. Temperature is 37.4 C, heart rate 82/min, and blood pressure 128/78 mm Hg. He has no medical history and takes no medications. He developed a rash after taking a sulfonamide antibiotic in the past. White blood cell count is 9,800/mm3.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: Incision and drainage of the affected area

imaging: Bedside soft-tissue ultrasound: subcutaneous edema, no fluid collection

vignette: A 19-year-old woman presents with 2 days of sore throat and fever. Temperature is 38.6 C. Examination shows tonsillar swelling with exudates and tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy; she has no cough. A rapid streptococcal antigen test is positive. She had anaphylaxis after receiving penicillin as a child. She takes no medications and is otherwise healthy.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

vignette: A 29-year-old man presents with 3 days of productive cough, fever, and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. He has no medical history, takes no medications, has no drug allergies, and has not received antibiotics in the past 3 months. Temperature is 38.4 C, heart rate 96/min, respiratory rate 20/min, blood pressure 124/76 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. He is alert and oriented. Chest x-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation. Blood urea nitrogen is 12 mg/dL.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate management?

options.text: Hospital admission for intravenous ceftriaxone and azithromycin

imaging: Chest x-ray: right lower lobe consolidation

vignette: A 24-year-old woman twisted her right ankle in an inversion injury while playing basketball 3 hours ago. She was able to walk four steps immediately after the injury and again in the emergency department. There is swelling and tenderness over the anterior talofibular ligament, but no bone tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of either malleolus, the navicular, or the base of the fifth metatarsal. Neurovascular examination is normal. She takes no medications and has no allergies.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?

options.text: Rest, ice, compression, elevation, and early mobilization without imaging

vignette: A 28-year-old woman reports 3 months of fatigue. She has heavy menstrual periods lasting 7 days. She eats a mixed diet and has no gastrointestinal symptoms. She takes no medications and has no allergies. Examination shows conjunctival pallor. Hemoglobin is 10.1 g/dL, mean corpuscular volume 72 fL, ferritin 7 ng/mL, and vitamin B12 is normal. Urine pregnancy test is negative.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial treatment?

vignette: A 45-year-old woman reports 4 months of fatigue, a 4-kg weight gain, constipation, and cold intolerance. She has no other medical history, takes no medications, and has no allergies. Heart rate is 58/min. Examination shows dry skin and delayed relaxation of the ankle reflexes. TSH is 14.2 mU/L (normal 0.4-4.0) and free T4 is 0.6 ng/dL (normal 0.8-1.8). Anti-thyroid peroxidase antibodies are positive.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

options.text: No treatment; repeat TSH in 12 months

vignette: A 52-year-old man wakes with severe pain, swelling, and redness of the right first metatarsophalangeal joint after drinking several beers the night before. He has no other medical history, takes no medications, and has no allergies. Temperature is 37.3 C. Serum creatinine is 0.9 mg/dL. Arthrocentesis shows needle-shaped, negatively birefringent crystals, and Gram stain shows no organisms.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment for this acute episode?

options.text: Allopurinol as the only treatment for the flare

labs.value: needle-shaped negatively birefringent crystals; Gram stain negative

vignette: A 60-year-old woman reports 1 week of brief episodes of intense vertigo, each lasting less than a minute, triggered by rolling over in bed and looking up. She has no hearing loss, tinnitus, headache, or focal weakness, and her neurologic examination is normal. The Dix-Hallpike maneuver with the head turned to the right reproduces the vertigo with upbeating, torsional nystagmus after a few seconds of latency. She has hypertension treated with amlodipine and no allergies.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?

vignette: A 72-year-old woman is found to have atrial fibrillation at a routine visit. She has hypertension and type 2 diabetes. Medications are lisinopril, metformin, and metoprolol, which was started last week and has controlled her heart rate to 78/min. Blood pressure is 132/80 mm Hg. ECG shows an irregularly irregular rhythm without P waves. Transthoracic echocardiography shows normal valves and a normal ejection fraction. eGFR is 70 mL/min/1.73 m2 and hemoglobin is 13.2 g/dL. She has no history of bleeding and no allergies.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate long-term therapy to prevent stroke?

options.text: Left atrial appendage occlusion as first-line therapy

imaging: ECG: irregularly irregular rhythm without P waves, ventricular rate 78/min
Transthoracic echocardiogram: normal valves, ejection fraction 60%

vignette: A 64-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease comes for follow-up. Medications are metformin 500 mg twice daily, lisinopril, and atorvastatin. He has no allergies. Hemoglobin A1c is 8.2%. Serum creatinine is 2.6 mg/dL and eGFR is 24 mL/min/1.73 m2, down from 34 one year ago. Potassium is 4.7 mEq/L. Renal ultrasound shows small echogenic kidneys bilaterally without hydronephrosis.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate change to his diabetes management?

options.text: Increase metformin to 1000 mg twice daily
Discontinue metformin and start a GLP-1 receptor agonist such as dulaglutide

imaging: Renal ultrasound: small echogenic kidneys bilaterally, no hydronephrosis

She has no other medical history and no allergies. Blood pressure is 152/98 mm Hg on two readings. Urinalysis shows no proteinuria. Serum creatinine is 0.7 mg/dL and platelet count is 240,000/mm3. Obstetric ultrasound shows a single live intrauterine fetus with biometry consistent with dates.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate change to her antihypertensive therapy?

options.text: Continue lisinopril at the current dose

imaging: Obstetric ultrasound: single live intrauterine fetus, biometry consistent with 20 weeks

vignette: A 70-year-old man with atrial fibrillation and knee osteoarthritis reports worsening right knee pain over 2 months. He takes warfarin 5 mg daily; his INR has been stable and is 2.6 today. He has no liver disease and drinks no alcohol. He has no allergies. Knee radiograph shows medial joint-space narrowing and osteophytes. Serum creatinine is 1.0 mg/dL and liver enzymes are normal.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate oral analgesic to start?

imaging: Right knee radiograph: medial joint-space narrowing and osteophytes

vignette: A 22-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes presents with 1 day of nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, and polyuria after running out of insulin. She uses insulin glargine and insulin lispro and has no allergies. Heart rate is 118/min, blood pressure 98/60 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 28/min with deep breathing. Mucous membranes are dry. Glucose is 520 mg/dL, arterial pH 7.12, bicarbonate 9 mEq/L, anion gap 26, and potassium 4.9 mEq/L; serum and urine ketones are strongly positive. Urine pregnancy test is negative.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate initial step in management?

options.text: Intravenous insulin bolus before any fluid resuscitation
Subcutaneous insulin glargine and discharge home
Emergency CT scan of the head

vignette: A 45-year-old woman presents with sudden pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea 2 days after a 14-hour flight. She takes a combined oral contraceptive and has no allergies. Heart rate is 112/min, blood pressure 128/80 mm Hg, respiratory rate 22/min, and oxygen saturation 92% on room air. The left calf is swollen and tender. ECG shows sinus tachycardia and chest x-ray is normal. Serum creatinine is 0.8 mg/dL and urine pregnancy test is negative. Her Wells score indicates that pulmonary embolism is likely.
question: Which of the following is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis?

vignette: A 66-year-old man with COPD presents with 3 days of increased dyspnea, increased sputum volume, and purulent sputum. He uses a tiotropium inhaler daily and albuterol as needed. He is allergic to penicillin (rash). Temperature is 37.8 C, heart rate 104/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 87% on room air. He has diffuse expiratory wheezes and speaks in full sentences. Arterial blood gas on room air shows pH 7.36, PaCO2 50 mm Hg, and PaO2 56 mm Hg. Chest x-ray shows hyperinflation without consolidation.

options.text: Inhaled short-acting bronchodilators, oral prednisone for 5 days, and oral doxycycline
Nebulized bronchodilators alone, without systemic corticosteroids or antibiotics

options.text: Intravenous fluid bolus of 3 L as the only treatment

imaging: Non-contrast CT abdomen and pelvis: 4-mm left distal ureteral stone, mild hydronephrosis

vignette: A 62-year-old man with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and type 2 diabetes presents with 1 hour of substernal chest pressure radiating to the jaw. He took sildenafil 12 hours ago. imaging: ECG: 2-mm horizontal ST depression V4-V6, no ST elevation

Omeprazole, bismuth subsalicylate, tetracycline, and metronidazole for 14 days
